title: A lymphoma fatigue programme, a preeclampsia test, and a way past the brain barrier
dek: A 150-person trial finds a 12-week programme eases lymphoma fatigue, but not by 9 months. Placental markers cut severe preeclampsia in one cohort. Also: laser heat opens the brain barrier in glioma mice, and a mouse stroke study.

tldr.text: In 150 lymphoma survivors with long-lasting fatigue, a 12-week programme lowered fatigue scores by 3.5 points at 3 months, but the gap faded by 9 months.
With biomarker-guided delivery, progression to severe preeclampsia fell from 52.1 percent to 19.6 percent in a before and after comparison.
In glioblastoma mice, mild laser heating opened the blood-brain barrier briefly and median survival rose to 36 days from 16 days.
In 13 mice after a stroke, stimulating the cerebellum raised motor cortex activity and improved recovery on a rotating beam task.
Cord blood levels of two neonicotinoid insecticide markers were linked to slower thinking in 9-year-olds, in a study of 200 samples.

top.title: A 12-week programme eased lingering fatigue in lymphoma survivors, but not for long
top.gist: In 150 lymphoma survivors with long fatigue, a 12-week programme cut scores by 3.5 points on a 0 to 33 scale at 3 months. By 9 months the gain was gone.

evidence.limitation: The benefit shrank to a non-significant 0.9 points by 9 months. Read from the abstract only.

top.why: Fatigue after cancer is common and hard to treat. A randomised trial shows a combined programme can help, and also shows that the help needs a way to last.
details: The programme combined patient education, physical exercise, a cognitive-behavioural therapy based programme and nutritional counselling. The comparison group received usual care.

Fatigue was lower than usual care by 3.5 points at 3 months (95 percent confidence interval, 1.6 to 5.4 points lower) and by 2.4 points at 6 months. At 9 months the gap was 0.9 points, with an interval that crossed zero.
At 3 months the programme also improved physical functioning, role functioning and global health. It did not clearly change social, emotional or cognitive functioning.
top.didNotShow: It did not show a lasting effect at 9 months, or which part of the programme did the work.

terms.def: A cancer of the lymph system, part of the body's immune network.
A questionnaire that scores physical and mental fatigue on a scale from 0 to 33.

top.title: Biomarker-guided delivery cut progression to severe preeclampsia in a before and after comparison
top.gist: At two hospitals, progression to severe preeclampsia fell from 52.1 percent with waiting to 19.6 percent with delivery guided by placental blood markers. Newborn outcomes were mixed.

evidence.limitation: Not randomised, with different years compared (2014 to 2017 versus 2022 to 2025). The authors say it was not powered to show newborn noninferiority.

top.why: Late preterm preeclampsia forces a hard choice between early birth and waiting. A blood test might help decide, but a randomised trial result still needs to hold up in routine care.
details: Women with preeclampsia without severe features at 34 to 36 weeks were compared. In the earlier period they were managed by waiting. In the later period delivery was advised when a placental marker profile was abnormal.

The adjusted odds ratio for severe progression was 0.22 (95 percent confidence interval, 0.13 to 0.38). Composite newborn illness fell from 57.0 percent to 45.6 percent, driven by fewer newborn unit admissions.
Newborn illness without counting admission was 35.2 percent and 35.6 percent, so the abstract shows no clear newborn gain beyond that.
top.didNotShow: It did not show that newborns fare as well as with waiting, because the study was not designed to test that.

top.title: A custom MRI method aims to show within weeks whether pancreatic cancer treatment works
top.gist: Ohio State researchers say a corrected MRI at 7 weeks of chemotherapy predicted response at 17 weeks. Standard CT at about 8 weeks caught response in 17 percent of patients.

evidence.limitation: Read from a Medical Xpress release. Patient numbers were not stated, and the 98 percent accuracy is an upper figure.

top.why: About 60 percent of people with pancreatic cancer cannot have surgery at diagnosis. Knowing early whether chemotherapy works would help decide who goes on to surgery.
details: The article describes a dynamic contrast enhanced MRI scan, corrected with a calibration object called a phantom. It reports accuracy of up to 98 percent in an earlier prospective study.

A new trial, NCT07705919, plans 50 people with pancreatic cancer judged resectable after pre-surgical treatment. It asks whether having the MRI information raises the rate of complete surgical removal. The registry record was not checked.
top.didNotShow: It did not show results from the new trial, or how many patients the earlier study included.

top.title: A genetic study of over 1 million people links 58 genome regions to endometriosis
top.gist: A multi-ancestry analysis across 14 biobanks found 58 genome regions tied to endometriosis, 27 of them new, and 314 implicated genes. Case numbers were not in the news report.

evidence.limitation: Read from a Medical Xpress report. Case and control counts and limitations were not stated.

top.why: Endometriosis takes years to diagnose and has few treatments. Genetic links point to pathways that drugs might reach, and to overlap with 135 other conditions or traits.
details: The report says the analysis covered more than 1 million participants, over 30 percent of non-European ancestry. Wider ancestry makes the findings useful for more people.
The team combined the genetic scan with other molecular data to name 314 genes. These are candidates, not proven causes.
top.didNotShow: It did not show which genes cause the disease or whether any is a good drug target.

top.title: Insecticide markers in cord blood were linked to slower thinking at age 9
top.gist: In 200 cord blood samples, higher levels of two neonicotinoid markers went with lower scores on two thinking tests at age 9. No link appeared in early childhood.

evidence.limitation: The authors cite a small sample and low concentrations. Effect sizes were not given in the news report.

top.why: Neonicotinoids are widely used insecticides that break down slowly. Small cohorts like this cannot prove harm, but they show where larger studies should look.
details: Ten neonicotinoid-related compounds were measured. Dinotefuran and desmethyl-acetamiprid were found in more than half of samples.

At 10 to 32 months there were no links after correcting for multiple comparisons. At age 9, more dinotefuran went with lower processing speed, and more desmethyl-acetamiprid with lower perceptual reasoning.
top.didNotShow: It did not show that the insecticides caused the lower scores, and gave no effect sizes in the report.

bench.title: Vascular-targeted mild photothermal modulation of the blood-brain barrier enables efficient delivery of Pt(IV) prodrug to glioblastoma
bench.headline: Gentle laser heating briefly loosened the blood-brain barrier in glioma mice, let 4.6 times more platinum into the tumour and lengthened survival.

evidence.limitation: One mouse glioma model. Group sizes and full text were not read.
evidence.conflicts: The authors declare no competing financial interests.

bench.question: Can mild heat open the barrier around a brain tumour just enough for a platinum drug to get in, without harming normal brain?
bench.approach: The team built nanoparticles with a near-infrared heat-making polymer, a platinum prodrug and a vessel-seeking peptide. They shone an 808 nm laser at the tumour.
bench.model: Mice with GL261 glioma tumours grown in the brain, plus cell work.
bench.result: At 0.5 W/cm2 for 3 minutes the tumour reached 46.3 °C. Six minutes reached 63 °C and activated glial cells. Permeability peaked at 1 hour and was near baseline by 24 hours. Platinum in the tumour rose about 4.6-fold. Median survival was 36 days versus 16 days for PBS.
bench.limitations: Mouse data from one model, read from the abstract. Group sizes and long-term safety were not checked.
bench.meaning: It supports the idea of a controllable thermal dose window for barrier opening, which other nanoparticle and phototherapy designs could borrow.

diagram.caption: Median survival in glioma mice was 36 days with the full system and laser, against 16 days for PBS.

terms.def: The most common and aggressive type of primary brain cancer.
A tight lining of the brain's blood vessels that limits which molecules enter the brain.
Using light absorbed by a material to make heat.
A drug given in an inactive form that is switched on at the target.

sources.label: Journal of Controlled Release, Chen et al.

bench.forYou: Mild photothermal dose windows and nanoparticle delivery across vascular barriers, relevant to tumour penetration.

bench.title: Cerebellar optogenetic stimulation restores motor cortex activity and behaviour after stroke
bench.headline: In mice, light stimulation of a cerebellar nucleus after a stroke raised motor cortex activity and improved recovery, whatever the size of the stroke.

evidence.model: Awake mice after transient middle cerebral artery occlusion
evidence.limitation: Small mouse study with 13 animals, followed for 28 days. Group sizes were not given.

bench.question: Can stimulating a distant brain region, the cerebellum, help the damaged motor cortex recover after a stroke?
bench.approach: The team imaged calcium activity in motor cortex neurons over time in awake mice. Treated mice got light stimulation of the opposite cerebellar nucleus on days 5 to 14.
bench.model: Mice with a temporary blockage of a brain artery, imaged with a head-mounted microscope.
bench.result: Stroke lowered cortical activity: peak frequency fell (p < 0.001) and amplitude fell (p = 0.004). Lower frequency tracked lesion size (r2 = 0.88). Stimulation raised frequency (p = 0.017) and amplitude (p < 0.001) and improved rotating beam performance (p = 0.027).
bench.limitations: Mouse data, read from the abstract. The rotating beam task is one behaviour. Whether it works in people is untested.
bench.meaning: It shows a remote brain region may be a stimulation target after stroke, and that recovery could be uncoupled from injury size.

terms.def: A method that makes neurons respond to light so researchers can switch them on.
A brain region at the back of the head that helps coordinate movement.
The brain area that plans and sends out voluntary movement commands.
A way to watch neurons fire by tracking a calcium-sensitive glowing dye.

learn.question: What does the blood-brain barrier block, and how can drugs get past it?
learn.answer: It is a tight lining of the brain's blood vessels that lets in nutrients but keeps out most drugs. Ways in include carrier proteins, brief heat or ultrasound, and targeted particles.
learn.analogy: Like a nightclub door with a guest list: small and approved molecules enter, most others stay outside.
body: Cells in the vessel wall are sealed by tight junction proteins, and pumps push many drugs back out. Most large molecules and many small ones never reach brain tissue.
In brain tumours the barrier is leaky in places, but unevenly, so drugs still reach the tumour poorly. Researchers try to open it briefly or to ride its carrier proteins.
In today's bench paper, mild laser heating reorganised two tight junction proteins for about a day, and platinum entered the tumour at 4.6 times the usual level in mice.

diagram.caption: A drug in the blood must cross sealed vessel cells and efflux pumps before it can reach brain tissue.

curiosity.title: Testosterone for women's libido is rising in use, but no product is approved
curiosity.gist: Science News reports that off-label testosterone prescriptions for women rose from 0.4 to 1.8 per 1,000 women between 2018 and 2026, while the research has not caught up.
body: Science News reports that the US Food and Drug Administration has not approved any testosterone product for women's sexual desire. Prescribing is off-label, using products made for men or compounded.

The article cites a 2008 trial in postmenopausal women that improved sexual function and desire, and says evidence in premenopausal women is preliminary. Large placebo effects and unresolved breast cancer and heart risks are noted.

evidence.limitation: Read from a Science News report, not from the papers it cites. No trial sizes or effect sizes were given.
